c.tagline: The world's southernmost city, wedged between the Beagle Channel and the Martial Mountains, gateway to Antarctica

card: Widely accepted; cash (preferably USD for exchange) useful for smaller shops

taxi.fareNote: Remis (pre-booked car services) are common alongside metered taxis

emergency.note: 911 is the general emergency line in most of Argentina; 107 specifically reaches medical services

walk: Central Ushuaia's port and main street are walkable; Tierra del Fuego National Park and the Martial Glacier require a car, bus, or tour

safety.safety: Very safe city, though weather can change rapidly and affect outdoor plans
safety.crime: Minimal crime; the main risks are weather-related for hikers and boat excursions

hood_landmark.Port / Downtown (San Martin Ave): Ushuaia's port and San Martín Avenue, the main commercial strip
hood_landmark.Martial Glacier Area: The Martial Glacier chairlift and hiking trails
hood_landmark.Bahia Cauquen: The Beagle Channel pebble beach at Bahia Cauquen

hood_desc: The compact downtown along the port, with most hotels, restaurants, and Antarctica expedition departure points.
A glacier and hiking area just above town, reachable by chairlift or on foot for panoramic views over the Beagle Channel.

A residential barrio on the Beagle Channel beach about 7 km west of the centre, reached by Ruta 3; it is the only shoreline stretch outside town where you can walk straight from your room onto the pebble beach, and you need a taxi or the hotel shuttle to reach the port and San Martin.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink in Ushuaia.

transit.map: Not centrally published; taxis and tours are common for reaching outlying sites
transit.note: Most excursions (national park, glacier, boat tours) are arranged through tour operators

transport.air: Ushuaia - Malvinas Argentinas International Airport (USH), about 10 min from downtown
transport.train: The End of the World Train is a tourist steam railway within Tierra del Fuego National Park, not a commuter service
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Rio Grande and onward to mainland Argentina/Chile
transport.ferry: Antarctica expedition cruises depart from Ushuaia's port (Oct-Mar season)
transport.car: Rental cars available; National Route 3 connects Ushuaia to the rest of Tierra del Fuego

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, limited in the national park
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Movistar, Claro, or Personal tourist SIM or eSIM

food.name: Centolla
food.desc: Southern king crab from the Beagle Channel, served natural with lemon, in a gratin, or as ravioli and empanada fillings. The dish that defines Ushuaia.

places.name: El Viejo Marino
places.note: Owner is a crab fisherman, so the centolla comes straight off his own boat; famously fresh.

places.name: Tia Elvira
places.note: Serving centolla since 1978 with channel views; garlicky shellfish starters are a highlight.

places.name: Kaupe
places.note: Hillside classic; centolla tapas served natural or with a passion-fruit sauce.

food.name: Cordero fueguino
food.desc: Fuegian lamb splayed on an iron cross and roasted slowly over open fire, or slow-cooked into a winter cazuela. Grass-fed and famously mild.

places.name: Kaupe
places.note: Does a warming cazuela de cordero fueguino alongside its seafood menu.

places.name: Bodegon Fueguino
places.note: Restored 1896 pioneer house specialising in regional lamb dishes and slow-cooked stews.

places.name: La Estancia
places.note: Central parrilla with lamb turning on the cross in the window; whole and half portions.

food.name: Merluza negra
food.desc: Patagonian toothfish, rich and buttery, usually pan-roasted with a light cream or citrus sauce. The local white fish worth ordering over salmon.

places.name: Tia Elvira
places.note: The tender merluza negra is often rated better than the crab; long-running family kitchen.

places.name: Kalma Resto
places.note: Ushuaia's most ambitious modern kitchen, built on Fuegian fish and foraged ingredients.

places.name: Reinamora
places.note: Local-produce menu of centolla and merluza negra with big channel views.

food.name: Mussels and cholgas from the Beagle Channel
food.desc: Cold-water mussels and giant cholgas steamed with white wine and garlic, or baked with breadcrumbs, pulled from the channel just offshore.

places.name: El Viejo Marino
places.note: Simple seafood house where shellfish plates arrive straight from local boats.

places.name: Volver
places.note: Century-old tin-clad house crammed with memorabilia; strong on channel shellfish.

places.name: Reinamora
places.note: Seasonal shellfish starters showcasing what came in that morning.

food.name: Fuegian artisan chocolate
food.desc: Ushuaia has a Bariloche-style chocolate tradition: hand-filled bombones, chocolate bars and alfajores made in small local workshops.

places.name: Laguna Negra
places.note: Chocolate and regional-produce shop with a cafe counter; popular for bombones and gifts.

places.name: Tante Sara
places.note: Local chain cafe and chocolate shop, good for alfajores and a warm-up stop.

places.name: Almacen Ramos Generales
places.note: Historic general-store cafe and bakery, an Ushuaia institution for sweets and coffee.

food.name: Calafate berry desserts
food.desc: The Patagonian barberry turned into mousse, ice cream and jams; legend says eating calafate guarantees you will return to Patagonia.

places.name: Laguna Negra
places.note: Sells calafate jams and sweets alongside its chocolate range.

places.name: Almacen Ramos Generales
places.note: Bakery cases with calafate tarts and regional preserves in a heritage setting.

places.name: Kalma Resto
places.note: Fine-dining desserts built on calafate and other native Fuegian berries.

food.name: Submarino
food.desc: Argentina's beloved hot chocolate: a bar of chocolate dropped into a glass of steaming milk and stirred until it melts. Essential in Ushuaia weather.

places.name: Almacen Ramos Generales
places.note: Wood-panelled cafe that is the classic spot for a submarino and medialunas.

places.name: Tante Sara
places.note: Reliable central cafe pouring submarinos all day, with its own chocolate.

places.name: Laguna Negra
places.note: Cafe counter inside the chocolate shop; hot chocolate made with their own bars.

food.name: Fuegian craft beer
food.desc: End-of-the-world breweries pour stouts, ambers and IPAs, several using glacial meltwater and calafate berries. Cerveza Beagle is the local name to look for.

places.name: Cerveceria Beagle taproom
places.note: Tierra del Fuego's best-known brewery; look for its beers on tap across town.

places.name: Dublin Irish Pub
places.note: Long-standing Ushuaia pub, packed with locals and crews, with local beers on tap.

places.name: Bodegon Fueguino
places.note: Regional restaurant that pairs Fuegian lamb with local craft beer.

landmarks: Tierra del Fuego National Park
Subantarctic forests, glacial lakes and windswept coast at the literal end of the Pan-American Highway, laced with trails just west of the city.
Beagle Channel and Les Éclaireurs Lighthouse
Cruise the legendary channel past sea-lion colonies to the red-and-white striped 'Lighthouse at the End of the World', Ushuaia's defining image.
Museo Marítimo y del Presidio
Housed in the notorious former prison that built the city, its radiating cellblocks now hold gripping maritime, Antarctic and convict-history exhibits.
End of the World Train (Tren del Fin del Mundo)
A narrow-gauge steam railway retracing the old prisoners' logging route through Pico Valley into Tierra del Fuego National Park.
Martial Glacier
The amphitheatre of peaks behind town hides this small glacier, reached by a stiff hike rewarded with immense views over Ushuaia and the Beagle Channel.
Laguna Esmeralda
A luminous emerald-green lagoon beneath jagged peaks, reached by a boggy, beautiful three-hour trail through lenga forest and beaver-dammed peat bogs.
Isla Martillo Penguin Colony
A Beagle Channel islet where thousands of Magellanic and gentoo penguins nest; small-group landings let you walk quietly among them.
Museo del Fin del Mundo
The 'End of the World Museum' gathers shipwreck relics, Yámana artefacts and stuffed birdlife that narrate Tierra del Fuego's wild frontier history.
Ushuaia Waterfront and 'Fin del Mundo' Sign
The bustling pier-side promenade where Antarctic expedition ships dock, framed by snowy peaks and the city's famous end-of-the-world sign.
Lago Escondido and Lago Fagnano
A scenic drive over Garibaldi Pass reveals these vast forest-ringed lakes, offering some of Tierra del Fuego's most photographed panoramas.

train.note: No international trains. The Tren del Fin del Mundo is the world's southernmost railway, a short narrow-gauge heritage line running into Tierra del Fuego National Park - it is a sightseeing ride of about an hour, not transport. Argentina's mainline network does not reach Tierra del Fuego at all. Arrive by coach or fly into Ushuaia airport.

intl.to: Punta Arenas (Chile) - via the Magellan Strait ferry, ~12 hr

intl.op: Bus Pacheco — tickets at the Ushuaia terminal

bus.note: Getting out of Ushuaia overland means crossing into Chile and back - the road runs through Chilean Tierra del Fuego and over the Primera Angostura ferry across the Magellan Strait, so the Punta Arenas coach takes about 12 hours with two border stops. Carry your passport and expect agricultural checks. Domestic buses reach Río Grande in 3-4 hours; book through Plataforma 10 (https://www.plataforma10.com.ar/).

intl.to: Puerto Williams (Chile) - across the Beagle Channel, ~1 hr
intl.op: Fernández Campbell / Ushuaia Boating — tickets at the Ushuaia pier or through local agents

ferry.note: The Puerto Williams crossing is a genuine international sailing and the only regular boat link between the two countries down here, taking about an hour across the Beagle Channel a few days a week in season - bring your passport and confirm the schedule, as it is weather-dependent and thin in winter. Ushuaia's port is otherwise the world's main Antarctic cruise base, with expedition sailings from October to March. Beagle Channel wildlife trips are excursions.

half.name: Estancia Harberton
half.blurb: Estancia Harberton is Tierra del Fuego's oldest ranch, founded by missionary Thomas Bridges, with historic buildings on the Beagle Channel shore.

full.name: Puerto Williams
full.blurb: Puerto Williams sits across the Beagle Channel from Ushuaia and is often called the southernmost town in the world.
